record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: In similarity languages such as CSL over R^n, suppose valuations of atomic terms are restricted so that each atomic predicate denotes a convex subset of R^n, or satisfies a comparable geometric restriction suggested by conceptual-space semantics. What are the computational properties of CSL and its extensions under these valuation restrictions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let CSL (the logic of comparative concept similarity) be the propositional modal-style language built from a countable set of propositional atoms by Boolean connectives together with a binary similarity connective ⇔, where a formula A ⇔ B is intended to express "the points satisfying A are at least as similar (close) to the current point as the points satisfying B are". Interpret CSL over R^n equipped with a fixed distance (e.g. the Euclidean metric, or more generally any metric or minspace structure on R^n), so that a valuation assigns to each atom p a subset V(p) ⊆ R^n, and the truth of x ⊨ A ⇔ B is defined in the standard way using infima of distances from x to V(A) and to V(B).

Now restrict the class of admissible valuations as follows: a valuation V is admissible iff for every atom p, the set V(p) is a convex subset of R^n (and more generally consider analogous geometric restrictions on V(p) suggested by conceptual-space semantics, such as being a convex polytope, a Voronoi cell, or a closed connected set).

Problem: Determine the computational properties — in particular, decidability and computational complexity of the satisfiability and validity problems — of CSL, and of natural extensions of CSL (for example with distance operators or with additional similarity comparators), interpreted over R^n under such convexity-type restrictions on the admissible valuations of atomic predicates.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search reveals work on CSL over minspaces and metric spaces (axiomatisation, tableaux calculi, ExpTime decidability) but no results addressing CSL or its extensions over R^n under convex-valuation (conceptual-space) restrictions. The computational status of CSL with such geometric restrictions on atomic valuations appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Comparative concept similarity over Minspaces: Axiomatisation and Tableaux Calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Axiomatisation and tableaux calculus for CSL over minspaces; addresses decidability over distance structures but not convex-valuation restrictions over R^n.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results address CSL over general minspaces/metric spaces, not under convex-valuation restrictions.

status_evidence.title: Tableau Calculus for the Logic of Comparative Similarity over Arbitrary Distance Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Develops tableau calculus for CSL over arbitrary distance spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Computational treatments of CSL focus on distance-space semantics, not the convex-valuation restriction.
